BenchClock is a time card for jewelry artists: clock in, work, clock out, and say what share of the session went to each piece on the bench. Everything stays on your own computer as plain files.

## Which file do I need?

| Your computer | Download |
| --- | --- |
| **Windows** 10 or 11 | the file ending in `win-x64.exe` |
| **Mac**, Apple Silicon or Intel | the file ending in `mac-universal.dmg` |
| **Linux**, Ubuntu, Debian, Mint | the file ending in `linux-amd64.deb` |
| **Linux**, anything else | the file ending in `.AppImage` (make it executable, then run it) |

## The first time you open it

BenchClock isn't signed with a paid certificate yet, so your computer will ask whether you trust it.

- **Windows** shows "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
- **Mac**: open the `.dmg` and drag BenchClock to Applications. If it is blocked when you open it, go to **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway**. On older versions of macOS, right-click the app and choose **Open**.

Updating is installing the new version over the old one. Your time card is kept separately and is not touched.

Inside the app, **Help > BenchClock Help** (F1) explains everything, and **Help > About BenchClock** shows the version you have.
